title: Protected wild plants
rule: The Minister may gazette a list of protected wild plants. Once listed, no one may pick, damage, destroy or otherwise interfere with them.
points: Publication of the list in the Gazette is itself what confers protection (s.67(2)).
Banned without lawful authority: picking, plucking, taking samples, or wilfully poisoning, damaging or destroying a listed plant (s.67(4)).
Where existing right holders in a forest reserve already use a listed plant, the Director must work with them on a scheme allowing continued, regulated use (s.67(5)).
The Director may grant a research permit to a qualified researcher with a reputable affiliation, allowing sampling of a listed plant (s.67(6)).
checks: Is the plant on a gazetted list
Lawful authority, licence or research permit
Existing right holder with an agreed scheme
